checkDefaults.failureBehavior: fail the applicable gate; no waiver, skip, quarantine, flaky-only pass, or unsupported not-applicable result
checkDefaults.cleanup: release handles and locks; retain only bounded sanitized evidence

checks.stimulus: exercise every version-1 handshake, control, query, command, event, payload bound, replay, collision, stale, gap, reload, and mismatch path through fake and production adapters
checks.oracle: the exact WF-020 catalog and generated schemas agree byte-for-byte across adapters; accepted commands produce equivalent authoritative transitions; invalid traffic has no side effect; snapshot-plus-events reconstruction matches host state

checks.setup: synthetic repository, resource corpus, MCP fixtures, deterministic model provider
checks.stimulus: discover valid, invalid, unavailable, changed, and conflicting resources; execute selection and snapshot boundaries
checks.oracle: validation, isolation, origin, precedence, effective model, and immutable snapshot match the specification

checks.setup: eligible/ineligible Agent matrices and deterministic Orchestrator fixture
checks.stimulus: select across zero, one, tied, overridden, declined, and twice-declined candidates
checks.oracle: hard eligibility, rationale, tie-break, proposal, mismatch cycle, one reroute, and append-only attempts are exact

checks.setup: model-based Task scheduler with generated contracts, dependencies, graphs, and locks
checks.stimulus: generate every valid and invalid WF-019 Task, Subtask, Assignment, lease, operation, compatibility, and migration transition plus admissions, graph revisions, dependencies, and concurrent schedules
checks.oracle: every canonical transition emits its exact event and atomic effects; every guard and terminal prohibition rejects without side effects; contract, DAG, readiness, one slot, concurrency three, and one-writer invariants always hold

checks.setup: real temporary SQLite, synthetic Git repository, deterministic crash controller
checks.stimulus: pause, cancel, force-stop, restart, drift, reconcile, retry, repair, and complete
checks.oracle: known checkpoint recovery, drift classification, no blind replay, bounded repair, and contract-based completion

checks.setup: real temporary SQLite, synthetic conversation and Tool fixtures
checks.stimulus: exercise every WF-019 Response Attempt transition and guard; create, send, stream, approve, block, fail, cancel, retry, interrupt, summarize, correct ledger, fork, trash, delete, and contend with Task lock
checks.oracle: exact Response state/event/capacity behavior, no resumed or outcome-unknown Response, fixed Agent, immutable attempts/history, visible provenance, non-cascade, correct context, and invocation-time lock behavior

checks.setup: path attack corpus, authority matrix, fake tools/providers, synthetic secrets and Git repository
checks.stimulus: attempt traversal, link escape, authority bypass, forbidden Git, secret capture, resource substitution, and uncertain retry
checks.oracle: every attempt is denied or safely executed within exact authority and produces sanitized append-only audit

checks.setup: synthetic tracked/untracked Memory corpus and provenance store
checks.stimulus: discover, promote, drift, conflict, retrieve, consolidate, hit capacity, interrupt commit, and reconcile
checks.oracle: schema/privacy, exact confirmation, provenance, conflict exclusion, ranking, capacity, lock, and recovery rules hold

checks.setup: all major Webview states in production CSP plus platform accessibility tooling
checks.stimulus: complete core flows keyboard-only; exercise focus, announcements, themes, zoom, motion, confirmations, badges, and notices
checks.oracle: WCAG 2.2 AA; automated scans clean; keyboard passes both targets; Narrator Windows and VoiceOver macOS attestations pass

checks.setup: real temporary databases for every released schema and corruption/interruption fixtures
checks.stimulus: generate and introspect schema v1; exercise all 60 command transaction classes, typed artifact references and cleanup, append-only guards, commit/rollback, direct migration, interruption, corruption, restore, reopen, and older code against newer schema
checks.oracle: all 59 tables, columns, constraints, triggers, 26 indexes, artifact-reference union, command coverage, authority separation, atomic event pairing, intent/result ordering, backup, integrity, refusal, and explicit recovery match the WF-021 machine contract

checks.setup: synthetic incidents with secrets, paths, identities, large evidence, and retention ages
checks.stimulus: derive health, persist incidents, project activity/output, expire evidence, create previewed bundles, and invoke recovery links
checks.oracle: metadata-only evidence, correct causal chain/retention, sanitized bundle, and read-only diagnostic boundary

checks.setup: two VSIXs built from one tagged revision and clean target runners
checks.stimulus: inspect, hash, scan, install, activate, restore, run packaged matrix, upgrade, downgrade, uninstall, and reinstall
checks.oracle: exact allowlist, same version/source, clean scans/SBOM/licenses, both target matrices pass, and publication is atomic

checks.stimulus: run the Specification Acceptance Gate validator and semantic checklist
checks.oracle: unique bidirectional complete traceability, all mandatory fields/coverage, zero unresolved items, and accountable acceptance record

acceptanceScenarios.initialState: clean synthetic repository containing independently valid, invalid, conflicting, unsupported, and unavailable resources
steps: start attempts across a resource edit boundary
oracle: each resource has the specified identity, origin, validity, availability, and diagnostic
one invalid resource does not disable unrelated resources except malformed top-level MCP JSON
each attempt retains its immutable Resource Snapshot and effective model
acceptanceScenarios.cleanup: stop synthetic MCP servers and remove the temporary workspace

acceptanceScenarios.initialState: empty workspace database and one valid Repository Agent
steps: trash and permanently delete only the origin
oracle: first Send creates durable Session and turn before model work
attempts and effective resources remain immutable
restart marks unfinished work interrupted without auto-resume
fork survives origin deletion with deleted-origin marker
acceptanceScenarios.cleanup: close attempts and remove temporary database/artifacts

acceptanceScenarios.initialState: Chat Session without Ambient Authority and a deterministic mutating Tool
steps: restart and reconcile applied, not-applied, and unknown variants
oracle: each request has a durable sanitized audit record
denial is side-effect-free
approved call stays within scope
retry occurs only after not-applied proof; unknown remains blocked
acceptanceScenarios.cleanup: reconcile or explicitly leave fixture outcome blocked, then delete temporary workspace

acceptanceScenarios.initialState: one running/queued expected-artifact fixture and one proposed Task draft
steps: independently confirm one dependency and deny one non-dependency
oracle: only named-artifact success dependency is proposed and stored
denial rationale persists
Task remains unqueued until the exact versioned contract and authority are confirmed
acceptanceScenarios.cleanup: cancel admitted synthetic Task and release slot/lock

acceptanceScenarios.initialState: confirmed Task with two independent read-only Subtasks, two write-capable Subtasks, and multiple eligible Agents
steps: run ready read-only work in parallel
perform Completion Check and one repair revision
oracle: no more than three attempts and one writer run
selection rationale and attempts persist
only success unlocks dependents
completed work is immutable
completion follows Task Contract
acceptanceScenarios.cleanup: finish Task and verify lock/slot release

acceptanceScenarios.initialState: three confirmed queued Tasks where the earliest is dependency-blocked and the later two are ready
steps: remove or replace dependency by explicit user action
oracle: single Active Task Slot is always unique
scheduler skips blocked earlier Task and starts earliest ready Task
failed prerequisite never satisfies dependency
order never overrides readiness
acceptanceScenarios.cleanup: cancel remaining synthetic Tasks and verify no slot owner

acceptanceScenarios.initialState: running Task with committed checkpoint, baseline, and Repository Write Lock
steps: modify repository with unrelated then conflicting drift variants
oracle: paused Task stays paused across restart
completed effects and checkpoint persist
unrelated drift refreshes context
conflict enters externally-blocked
safe resume reacquires lock only after revalidation
acceptanceScenarios.cleanup: cancel or complete recovered Task and remove fixture

acceptanceScenarios.initialState: one deterministic fixture per registered Durability Boundary
steps: inject termination immediately before and after each boundary
classify resumed, reconciled, blocked, or terminal result
oracle: every registered boundary is exercised
committed state survives and incomplete transactions roll back
effect handoff is reconciled
no stale lock or unresolved outcome advances
acceptanceScenarios.cleanup: resolve fixture operations and delete each temporary database/repository

acceptanceScenarios.initialState: active Chat Session and Task ready to acquire Repository Write Lock
steps: send Chat read-only and mutation-seeking turns
oracle: Task waits for active mutation safe boundary
pending Chat approval does not delay lock
Chat conversation/read Tools continue under lock
write/opaque calls deny at invocation and are not queued
mutation returns after release
acceptanceScenarios.cleanup: finish Chat attempt and Task; verify global writer idle

acceptanceScenarios.initialState: recoverable Task fixture with switchable drift, authority, model, MCP, and operation conditions
steps: activate recovery or next scheduling boundary
oracle: each condition maps to specified blocked, routing, or failed state
no authority prompt interrupts Task execution
unknown operation requires reconciliation
restored conditions are revalidated before resume
acceptanceScenarios.cleanup: restore fixtures, resolve notices, and terminate Task

acceptanceScenarios.initialState: valid Project/Personal Memories plus stale, conflicting, capacity, tracked-personal, and interrupted-write variants
oracle: rejection writes nothing
confirmation hash binds exact content/scope
tracked Personal Memory blocks
conflict excludes guidance
consolidation preserves provenance
recovery never blindly replays
acceptanceScenarios.cleanup: reconcile fixture and remove synthetic Memory files/provenance

acceptanceScenarios.initialState: every major Workbench state with deterministic Tasks, Chats, interventions, recovery, and diagnostics
steps: exercise composite navigation and focus restoration
toggle zoom, contrast, and reduced motion
run automated semantics; run packaged Narrator and VoiceOver representative flows
oracle: WCAG 2.2 AA semantics and keyboard behavior pass
focus never moves from background work
announcements are polite and deduplicated
badge counts unresolved requests only
platform attestations pass
acceptanceScenarios.cleanup: resolve Attention Requests and close Webview fixtures

acceptanceScenarios.initialState: fresh, every prior schema, interrupted/corrupt migration, valid backup, and newer-schema database variants
steps: inject interruption at each migration boundary
run older code against newer schema
oracle: writable services wait for compatibility
migration is transactional and direct
live database/backup survive failure
recovery is explicit
older code refuses every write
acceptanceScenarios.cleanup: close connections and delete synthetic database/backup files

acceptanceScenarios.initialState: each authoritative Task, Chat, Agent, Memory, attention, diagnostics, migration, and recovery presentation state
steps: send stale old-instance and duplicate messages
oracle: new projection equals host authoritative state
ephemeral view preferences may restore separately
old-instance, stale, duplicate, and mismatched inputs have deterministic side-effect-free outcomes
acceptanceScenarios.cleanup: dispose both Webview instances and temporary workspace

attackerCapabilities: malicious prompt or Agent supplies crafted paths
repository content retargets or introduces links
abusePaths: absolute, drive, UNC, device, parent traversal
requiredControls: canonical Repository Boundary validation on every source and destination
link target binding and retarget invalidation
threatCases.acceptedResidualRisk: A separately authorized Ambient Tool may act outside the Repository Boundary with the local user's authority; the Authority Review discloses that it is not sandboxed.

attackerCapabilities: stale or forged approval is replayed
threatCases.acceptedResidualRisk: A user may knowingly authorize broad Task external capability or arbitrary shell after the required disclosure; Bridgit cannot sandbox those effects.

attackerCapabilities: Tool or error returns secret-like content
threatCases.acceptedResidualRisk: An authorized Ambient Tool may independently use credentials available to the local user; Bridgit neither retrieves nor guarantees containment of that external process.
A user-authorized repository edit may intentionally change resources for the next snapshot; active attempts retain the prior validated version.

attackerCapabilities: stale source conflicts with current repository
threatCases.acceptedResidualRisk: The user may explicitly confirm incorrect but schema-valid guidance; provenance keeps that decision inspectable and later correction supersedes it.
A local user or host failure can destroy both live database and backup; the MVP provides recovery checks, not tamper-proof or off-device storage.

attackerCapabilities: craft identifiers that resemble safe metadata
threatCases.acceptedResidualRisk: A user can deliberately include previewed content in one local bundle; that explicit one-bundle choice is not reusable consent.

attackerCapabilities: diagnostic action tries to mutate history
threatCases.acceptedResidualRisk: The MVP does not provide cryptographic tamper evidence against a local user with direct storage access; corruption is detected where integrity checks can observe it.
Scanning cannot prove the absence of unknown vulnerabilities; known exploitable shipped high or critical findings block release.

durabilityBoundaries.point: transaction committing a confirmed Task Contract before queue admission
durabilityBoundaries.expectedRecovery: contract is wholly admitted or absent

durabilityBoundaries.point: transaction committing a Task Graph Revision and audit event
durabilityBoundaries.expectedRecovery: revision and current graph agree, or neither changed

durabilityBoundaries.point: transaction committing selected Agent, rationale, and Resource Snapshot before execution
durabilityBoundaries.expectedRecovery: attempt is durably selected or nonexistent

durabilityBoundaries.point: transaction committing submitted user turn before model or Tool work
durabilityBoundaries.expectedRecovery: one durable turn exists and unfinished attempt may retry without duplicating it

durabilityBoundaries.point: transaction committing mutation intent and Operation Key before external handoff
durabilityBoundaries.expectedRecovery: operation is known pending and must reconcile before retry

durabilityBoundaries.point: immediate boundary where a committed operation is handed to a repository, Tool, MCP, or external provider
durabilityBoundaries.expectedRecovery: outcome is reconciled as applied, not applied, or unknown

durabilityBoundaries.point: transaction committing observed operation result and audit evidence
durabilityBoundaries.expectedRecovery: committed outcome is authoritative and effect is not replayed

durabilityBoundaries.point: transaction committing continuation state after completed effects
durabilityBoundaries.expectedRecovery: Runtime resumes only from the complete checkpoint

durabilityBoundaries.point: transaction committing Repository Write Lock ownership before Task mutation
durabilityBoundaries.expectedRecovery: at most one owner is visible; uncommitted acquisition owns nothing

durabilityBoundaries.point: transaction committing lock release after quiescence or non-executing transition
durabilityBoundaries.expectedRecovery: no stale owner remains after committed release; interrupted release is recovered before work

durabilityBoundaries.point: transaction committing exact confirmed Memory proposal hash and Operation Key
durabilityBoundaries.expectedRecovery: only the confirmed version may proceed and drift invalidates it

durabilityBoundaries.point: handoff applying recoverable exact Memory file replacement
durabilityBoundaries.expectedRecovery: file is reconciled against intended postcondition before retry

durabilityBoundaries.point: transaction pairing reconciled Memory version with private provenance and registry refresh
durabilityBoundaries.expectedRecovery: file, provenance, and registry are reconciled or explicitly blocked

durabilityBoundaries.point: pre-upgrade backup checksum and source schema are committed before migration chain
durabilityBoundaries.expectedRecovery: migration never begins without one restorable verified backup

durabilityBoundaries.point: each registered schema migration step record inside the one ordered migration-chain transaction, keyed by source, target, migration, and step identity
durabilityBoundaries.expectedRecovery: the entire chain, including every step record, is wholly committed or rolled back and can be deterministically re-evaluated

durabilityBoundaries.point: post-chain integrity success and successful restart reopen before writable startup or backup replacement
durabilityBoundaries.expectedRecovery: failed verification blocks writes and preserves live database plus backup

durabilityBoundaries.point: explicit user-authorized replacement of live database from verified backup
durabilityBoundaries.expectedRecovery: old live database is preserved until restored database passes integrity and reopen checks
